current_role: U.S. Secretary of Defense, styled Secretary of War (since January 25, 2025)
summary: Pete Hegseth, a Princeton graduate and Army National Guard officer who served at Guantánamo Bay, in Iraq and in Afghanistan, led the advocacy groups Vets for Freedom and Concerned Veterans for America and was a Fox News contributor and host from 2014 to 2024. Trump chose him as defense secretary; the Senate confirmed him 51–50 on January 24, 2025, with JD Vance breaking the tie, and since September 2025 he also uses the title Secretary of War. He has overseen strikes on alleged drug boats from September 2025, the war with Iran that began on February 28, 2026, and the 2026 designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk. Rep. Thomas Massie filed impeachment articles against him in September 2026, and after Republicans lost Congress in November 2026 Trump said Hegseth would stay while reports said he was weighing a replacement.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Trump nominated Hegseth, then a Fox News host, as defense secretary; he was sworn in on January 25, 2025, and in September 2025 Trump's executive order let him use the title Secretary of War. On November 4, 2026, after Republicans lost Congress, Trump said Hegseth would stay on; CBS reported he was privately weighing a replacement.

connections.name: JD Vance
connections.description: Vance cast the tie-breaking vote that confirmed Hegseth 51–50 on January 24, 2025, only the second time a vice president has broken a tie on a cabinet nominee, and swore him in the next day; both serve in Trump's second administration. In the March 2025 Signal chat on the Houthi strikes, Vance argued for delaying them and Hegseth answered that he shared Vance’s view of European free-loading.
